mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month indicates a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a month signals a weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases > 2% in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% YoY, it indicates a low inflation and accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL YoY < 2% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.
